applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1994, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L.561-1 to L.561-57 and R.561-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Ordonnance n° 2020-1192 of 29 September 2020; Loi n° 2016-1691 of 9 December 2016 (Sapin II); Loi n° 2017-399 of 27 March 2017; Décret n° 2018-284 of 18 April 2018 on the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs; EU Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; Code de Commerce Articles R.123-58 et seq. regarding the RBE.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each shareholder and each ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary, commissioner of oaths, or issuing embassy/consulate in the shareholder's jurisdiction of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or official extract from foreign trade registry for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official company registrar of the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly signed Power of Attorney authorizing the French incorporation agent or avocat to file the registration and sign mandatory documents
Sworn French translation of each non-French document in the bundle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Traducteur expert sworn translator registered with a French Cour d'appel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Consular Legalization where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, statutory auditors, and signatories against the French asset-freeze decisions list maintained by the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List for any USD payment rails. PEP identification follows FATF Recommendation 12, EU Directive 2015/849 Article 3(9), and the guidance of the French Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority. The low-money-laundering-risk classification of a software publishing business does not exempt the mandatory customer due diligence and ongoing monitoring duties.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises (https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) operated by the INPI, with name-availability search through Infogreffe (https://www.infogreffe.fr) and the official RNE extract service (https://data.inpi.fr).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name (dénomination sociale) must be written in Latin characters for registration in the French Registre National des Entreprises. A name using non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin script. The name may be in a foreign language but must not be contrary to French public order, must not create confusion with a prior registered name or trademark, and must not imply a regulated activity. The legal form suffix 'SAS' or 'Société par actions simplifiée' must be used in the articles of association and on all formal documents.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A preliminary name-availability certificate obtained from Infogreffe or the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce is valid for 30 days and cannot be administratively extended; after expiry, a new availability check must be run. If the registered company name is rejected during formation, the applicant may first ask the Greffe to state its written grounds and may file a rectification through the Guichet Unique within 15 days. If the rejection is confirmed, a formal recours gracieux must be submitted to the same Greffe within 15 days, followed by an appeal to the competent Tribunal judiciaire (commercial chamber) within one month from notification of the rejection, under the procedure prescribed by Code de Commerce Articles R.123-20 et seq.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A fully virtual office is not permitted for the statutory registered office of a French SAS. The registered office must be a physical address in France where legal process can be served and the articles of association must state the exact address. Commercial domiciliation companies are permitted only if they hold the required approval and provide a physical reception office with actual mailing and document acceptance capacity, including the use of private-law service providers under Décret n° 2014-510, Article R.123-213. For the MMORPG publishing industry, remote operation is commercially acceptable, but a physical French registered office and demonstrable administrative substance remain mandatory for valid incorporation, tax residence, and VAT registration stability.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 15% to 20% annual probability of an unannounced inspection by tax administration or trade registry authorities for a new low-risk digital services company; the probability increases to approximately 35% to 40% if the registered office is a shared third-party domiciliation address with limited documented commercial substance.

Apostille / consular legalization of foreign corporate and identity documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff, approximately EUR 50-80 per page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bank account opening and minimum banking due diligence package
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French bank or licensed online payment institution
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published fee schedule, opening and first-month maintenance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN, France, and EU sanctions screening of all shareholders and UBOs

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), including Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.227-1 to L.227-20, R.123-1 et seq., and applicable provisions concerning beneficial-owner declarations. The SAS is also subject to the Civil Code provisions on companies and the French Monetary and Financial Code where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The competent commercial registry is the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by the locally competent commercial court registry (greffe du tribunal de commerce). Applications are submitted through the national Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic declaration of incorporation and registration formalité submitted through the Guichet unique, supported by the executed SAS articles of association, capital deposit certificate, beneficial-owner declaration, and required identification and premises documents.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital is required for an SAS; EUR 1 is legally sufficient, subject to commercial credibility and banking requirements. For cash contributions, at least 50% of subscribed share capital must be paid upon incorporation, with the balance payable within five years of registration. Funds are deposited into a blocked company-formation account, and the bank issues a certificate of deposit. Contributions in kind must be fully paid when subscribed and may require a commissaire aux apports report, subject to statutory exemptions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscription by the shareholder(s) for the shares specified in the articles of association and confirms the deposit of the required paid-up cash capital. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [full French address], effective upon registration. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President (Président) for the term and under the powers stated in the articles. RESOLVED, if applicable, that [Name] is appointed Directeur Général. The officers are authorised to complete all filings, banking arrangements, tax registrations, and formalities required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve corporate structure and SAS articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company founders, assisted by French counsel or a formation provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the company name, corporate purpose, share capital, share classes, transfer restrictions, governance rules, President, financial year, registered office, and beneficial owners. Prepare and sign the French-language articles of association. Obtain certified translations where foreign corporate documents are used.
required_dossiers: Draft and executed SAS articles of association
Foreign shareholder corporate certificates and powers of attorney, if applicable
Registered-office title, lease, domiciliation agreement, or host certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistent provisions, obtain missing signatures or translations, and re-execute the articles before filing. Ensure the President has expressly accepted office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open formation bank account and deposit capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank, payment institution, or authorised notarial deposit channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed draft articles, identification and know-your-customer documents, ownership chart, business plan, and registered-office evidence. Deposit the required cash capital into a blocked formation account and obtain the certificate of deposit. Do not use the funds for operating expenses before release after registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to bank compliance queries with source-of-funds evidence, corporate ownership documents, and translated or apostilled foreign records. If onboarding is refused, approach another authorised institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A journal d'annonces légales authorised in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the mandatory incorporation notice containing the company name, legal form, capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, President, and registration details required by applicable law. Pay the prescribed flat legal-notice fee and retain the publication certificate.
required_dossiers: Articles or extract of articles, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request correction or republication if the notice contains a material error. Upload the corrected publication certificate to the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by INPI
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create the electronic filing, select constitution of an SAS, complete the company, activity, premises, officers, shareholder, tax, and beneficial-owner fields, upload the required documents, electronically sign the declaration, and pay the applicable fees. The Guichet unique forwards the filing to the RCS and relevant administrations.
required_dossiers: Foreign corporate documents and powers of attorney, if applicable
Translation or apostille documents, where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Monitor the electronic filing dashboard and respond within the stated deadline to any request for regularisation. Replace defective scans, correct inconsistent data, and resubmit the queried items without changing the filing date unless instructed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain registration evidence and release capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial court registry and formation bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the SIREN and SIRET numbers, Kbis extract, and RCS registration confirmation after acceptance. Provide the registration evidence to the bank so the blocked capital account can be released into the SAS operating account.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract or RCS registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed, obtain the registry query or rejection notice and cure the specified defect. If the bank does not release funds, submit the Kbis and request formal escalation through its corporate-services department.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete post-registration tax and social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Service des impôts des entreprises (SIE), URSSAF, and other applicable French administrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm corporate income-tax and VAT treatment, activate the company tax account, establish payroll and social-security registrations if employees are hired, and implement accounting, invoicing, and statutory-record procedures. Register for VAT reporting before commencing taxable supplies where required.
required_dossiers: Employment and payroll information, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: File corrective tax or social declarations, contact the relevant SIE or URSSAF service, and document the effective date of commencement and any requested tax elections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement corporate governance and statutory records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company President and shareholders; commercial registry for subsequent statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the share register, shareholder decisions, board or management decisions required by the articles, accounting records, beneficial-owner records, contracts, and annual accounts. Record officer appointments, related-party agreements, capital changes, transfers, and amendments. File annual accounts and subsequent changes within statutory deadlines.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Adopt ratifying shareholder decisions, correct registers, file late or amended documents where permitted, and obtain professional advice for defective corporate acts or missed statutory deadlines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to ordinary software publishing and online MMORPG operations. If the company operates premises involving an industrial installation, the relevant authority is the Préfecture of the department under the Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement (ICPE) regime.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for publishing digital MMORPG software, in-app purchases, or receiving Apple App Store and Google Play payouts. General business, consumer, data-protection, copyright, platform, and e-commerce compliance remains applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for Ecological Transition (Ministère de la Transition écologique), with departmental prefectural services where an ICPE or environmental authorisation is relevant
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt or not applicable for ordinary office-based software publishing with no industrial plant, material emissions, wastewater process, or regulated storage. A project-specific screening is required if premises or infrastructure fall within an ICPE category.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No sector-specific industrial wastewater or VOC threshold applies to ordinary software publishing offices. The company must manage office waste through authorised channels, comply with applicable electrical and electronic equipment and battery waste rules, avoid unauthorised discharge, and obtain any required ICPE or environmental authorisation before operating regulated equipment or storage.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No manufacturing clearance is required for ordinary office and digital operations. The premises must satisfy applicable fire-safety and accessibility rules; an Établissement Recevant du Public (ERP) classification may trigger additional approval if the public is admitted. The landlord or operator should maintain fire equipment, evacuation plans, emergency access, electrical safety, and building structural compliance. Employers must prepare occupational-risk assessments, provide workplace safety measures, and complete required employee health and safety formalities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); web portal: www.impots.gouv.fr; local operational desk: Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE); national non-resident VAT registration unit for foreign entities; corporate income tax supervision for large groups: Direction des Grandes Entreprises (DGE); INSEE allocates SIREN/SIRET; e-invoicing transmission hub: Portail Public de Facturation (PPF).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity not established in France must apply for a French VAT identification number before its first taxable transaction by filing the statutory non-resident VAT registration application (form available on impots.gouv.fr, submitted to the competent SIE or the DGFiP national non-resident registration service); INSEE issues SIREN/SIRET for any French permanent establishment, and the intra-Community VAT ID is delivered in the format FR + 2-digit control key + 9-digit SIREN. For a French SAS, incorporation through the guichet unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) automatically generates the SIREN/SIRET and the NAF code 58.21Z (édition de jeux électroniques), following which the SIE activates the French VAT number. OSS (Union and non-Union) registrations for EU B2C digital services are filed electronically on the impots.gouv.fr one-stop-shop portal. Processing typically takes one to three weeks; a non-established foreign business may limit itself to OSS non-Union registration for EU B2C digital sales, but any French establishment, inventory, or B2B wholesale activity requires a full French VAT ID.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law contains no check-the-box election. The SAS is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) on worldwide profits under Article 206-1 CGI. Available elections: (i) the five-year option for personal income tax under Article 239 bis AB CGI for small SAS satisfying the SME criteria (≤50 employees, ≤EUR 10M turnover, capital held by individuals); (ii) French fiscal integration under Article 223 A CGI where a French parent holds at least 95% of the shares; (iii) the VAT One-Stop-Shop (Union and non-Union) schemes under Article 289 A CGI for B2C digital services; (iv) mandatory EU B2B reverse-charge allocation under Article 283-2 CGI (no election); and (v) no hybrid-mismatch election is available: France applies the ATAD anti-hybrid rules in Articles 212 bis and 239 CGI, and foreign check-the-box classifications of the SAS are disregarded for French tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA), codified at Articles 256 to 277 of the French General Tax Code (CGI), implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; supplemented by the mandatory e-invoicing and e-reporting reform introduced by the 2020 Finance Act (Article 289 bis et seq. CGI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero registration threshold for digital services: the SME VAT exemption (franchise en base de TVA, Article 293 B CGI) is excluded for electronically supplied services such as MMORPG content and in-app purchases, so the SAS must register for French VAT from the first taxable euro. For comparison, the 2025 franchise thresholds are EUR 91,900 for supply of goods and EUR 36,800 for services (upper limits EUR 101,000 and EUR 39,100 respectively). For intra-EU B2C digital supplies, the EUR 10,000 Union-wide threshold of Article 59 quinquies CGI applies: below it, French VAT is chargeable on all EU consumer sales; above it, OSS filing applies at the consumer's country rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France does not operate real-time fiscal stamping or transaction-clearance (CTC) approval. Under Articles 289 bis et seq. CGI, mandatory structured e-invoicing (Factur-X, UBL, or CII XML) and e-reporting are phased in: reception of e-invoices becomes mandatory for all enterprises on 1 September 2026; issuance and e-reporting become mandatory for large and mid-sized enterprises on 1 September 2026 and for all enterprises, including the SAS, on 1 September 2027. Invoices and transaction/payment data must be transmitted through an accredited dematerialization partner (PDP) or the State PPF via authenticated API flows; no digital stamp is affixed, but DGFiP receives structured taxable data in near-real time, enabling automated cross-checking of B2B, B2C, and export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of goods outside the EU are zero-rated VAT-exempt under Article 262-I-1° CGI provided the exporter proves physical departure from the EU within three months of supply. For the MMORPG activity, which is digital services rather than goods, the applicable framework is the territoriality rules of Articles 259, 259 A to 259 D CGI: (1) B2B digital services supplied to customers established outside France are outside French VAT (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction); (2) B2C digital services supplied to consumers outside the EU are outside French VAT; (3) B2C digital services supplied to EU consumers are taxable in the consumer's member state and may be declared under OSS; (4) app-store sales distributed through Apple App Store and Google Play are treated as deemed supplies by the marketplace operators, which collect and remit the VAT, the SAS receiving net-of-VAT proceeds while retaining its own French VAT registration and reporting duties for direct channels.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation DELTA, including the MRN movement reference number)
Commercial invoice in original, expressly stating the 0% VAT/exemption basis (Article 289 CGI)
Bill of Lading, CMR road consignment note, or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate and bank settlement records evidencing FX repatriation of export proceeds
Digital-services evidence pack: framework contract, delivery and server logs, customer IP address and BIC/SWIFT country data, and OSS quarterly returns for destination-state-taxed supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Unjustified export zero-rating or failure to produce the documentary proof bundle triggers immediate VAT repayment demand with retrospective clawback, late interest at 0.20% per month (Article 1727 CGI), and statutory penalties: 10% for late filing, 40% for deliberate inaccuracy (manvaise foi), and 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres (Articles 1728 and 1729 CGI). Criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI may result in fines up to EUR 750,000 (EUR 3 million with aggravating circumstances) and imprisonment of up to five years (seven years with aggravating circumstances). The DGFiP may reassess within three years (Articles L. 169 and L. 180 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales), extended to six years for undisclosed activities and ten years for unreported foreign assets or receivables (Articles L. 176 and L. 180 B LPF). VAT refund claims (crédit de TVA / remboursement) may be suspended pending complete substantiation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF), the French central bank and member of the Eurosystem/European Central Bank. Banking and e-money institutions are supervised by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR), with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) holding policy authority for foreign-exchange regulation and the screening of inward foreign direct investment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France observes full current-account and capital-account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF Articles of Agreement and Articles 63-66 TFEU. EUR-denominated operations within France are unrestricted, and non-EUR accounts (USD, JPY, KRW) can be opened freely at French banks. Capital-account formalities exist only for inbound foreign investment in sensitive sectors (defence, cybersecurity, dual-use, critical infrastructure and certain AI/R&D services) under Decrees 2019-1590 and 2023-1294; electronic game publishing (ISIC 5820) is not a regulated sector, so no prior IEF (Investissements Étrangers en France) approval is required for capital injection into the SAS. Profit remittance is not subject to foreign-exchange approval: the SAS may distribute dividends freely in EUR or foreign currency. The principal friction is tax: outbound dividends to corporate non-residents are normally subject to French withholding tax at 25% (Article 119 bis 2 CGI), reduced to 0% for a qualifying EU/EEA parent under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (minimum 10% holding and 2-year minimum holding period), or reduced under an applicable tax treaty; the bank will require the shareholder's certificate of tax residence and the SAS distribution resolution to apply the correct treaty rate.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or repatriation requirement exists. France abolished mandatory export-receipt surrender and conversion obligations in 1990, and as a euro-area member there is no central-bank rule requiring the SAS to convert USD or other foreign-currency proceeds into EUR, nor any statutory deadline for deposit of export receipts inside France. Proceeds may be held in multi-currency accounts in France or with an EU/EEA bank, or reinvested abroad, subject only to the corporate treasury policies of the SAS and the relevant tax rules. A statistical monitoring obligation remains under the Banque de France balance-of-payments framework: each cross-border payment of EUR 12,500 or more (and each remittance between a French resident and a non-resident) is reported by the client's bank using the client's stated purpose code; the SAS is legally required only to identify the nature of the transaction accurately on the payment order.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR account (compte de dépôt), multi-currency account (USD/JPY/KRW), and temporary blocked capital escrow account (compte bloqué) for the initial SAS incorporation capital deposit
Operational EUR account, multi-currency account, ancillary treasury lines, and host account for SAS incorporation funds; can support shareholder current accounts and cash pooling
Operational professional EUR account and dedicated shareholder current account; adequate regional coverage, less specialized video-gaming vertical
Operational EUR account and multi-currency accounts; strong for mid-size international corporate treasury and FX hedging

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High for French-licensed challenger banks (Qonto, Shine) as an operational account for an early-stage SAS; Medium for EEA-passported EMIs (Wise Business, Revolut Business, Airwallex) as secondary treasury rails; Low for offshore or non-EEA EMIs as the principal treasury bank. Legal constraints: an EMI incorporated outside the EEA cannot provide payment services or hold client funds in France without a full ACPR licence; an EEA EMI may only passport its licence into France under PSD2. The French Treasury (DGFiP) routes tax payments through French-regulated credit institutions, and the SAS's main corporate tax and VAT filings (via EBICS with ISO 20022) require an established French bank. An offshore EMI cannot provide a locally clearing French IBAN on Target-2/SEPA, cannot issue the required French BIC for French treasury operations, and is not accepted for cash-management arrangements. Recommended blueprint: principal operating account at a Tier-1 French bank, with EMIs used only for card programmes, vendor FX sweeps and ancillary collection of platform payouts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French Tier-1 banks normally require one physical KYC/onboarding interview with the legal representative of the SAS (the Président) or a person holding a valid Pouvoir (power of attorney) authenticated by the bank. Technical identification of directors and major shareholders may be performed remotely using live video, digital identity verification (France Identité) and secure document upload; however, final execution of the account agreement and issuance of signature cards and banking tokens usually triggers a branch appointment. Remote-only opening is available from ACPR-licensed online banks (Qonto, Shine, etc.) but is subject to lower transaction limits and lacks the correspondent network required for cross-border LC and FX lines. Recommended measures: have the Président or a local officer attend a single branch meeting in Paris or Lyon, or grant a power of attorney to a French-resident representative; this reduces onboarding from four to six weeks down to approximately seven to ten days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-transparent UBO chain: French AML law (Article L561-5 CMF) requires identification of every natural person holding more than 25% of shares or voting rights; an Asian or multi-tiered holding structure with non-resident UBOs triggers systematic enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration filed with the INPI through the guichet unique; notarized passports of all UBOs, apostilled and translated into French; shareholders' register; signed statement on the source of funds (attestation d'origine des fonds); corporate structure tree with exact ownership percentages; SAS articles of association (statuts) and certificate of registration (extrait Kbis).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound app-store revenue pattern: the bank sees high-frequency credits from Apple Distribution International (Ireland) and Google Payments (US/IRL/JPN) that do not match conventional B2B invoices, raising questions about in-app purchases, virtual currency or potential gambling flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Program License Agreement and Google Play Developer Distribution Agreement; App Store Connect and Play Console payout statements; daily or weekly platform settlement reports; PEGI age-rating certificate; proof that in-game virtual currency is non-redeemable for FIAT and that the game does not qualify as gambling under French law; VAT digital-services position and the SAS's declared revenue reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound vendor payments to foreign cloud and software suppliers (AWS Europe, Google Cloud, Equinix, game-lab developers in Asia) with ambiguous payment descriptions or destinations in mixed-use jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed vendor contracts and service-level agreements; itemized invoices with VAT/GST breakdown; purchase orders; evidence of service delivery (server logs, usage reports, support tickets); export-control classification (ECCN) for any cryptographic software; compliance statement under EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821; treasury cash-flow forecast matching each vendor.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) including balance sheet, income statement, and notes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after fiscal year-end; filing within 1 month of shareholder approval of accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing injunctions, civil fine up to EUR 1,000; persistent failure can trigger court-imposed strike-off (radiation) from RCS

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Shareholder annual approval of accounts (procès-verbal d'assemblée) and audit report submission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (via the annual accounts filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end (unless extended by court order)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene assembly can lead to civil penalties and judicial dissolution in severe cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner (UBO) annual confirmation / declaration of any change (déclaration de bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation at the time of annual accounts filing; any change within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000 for natural persons and EUR 25,000 for legal entities; potential imprisonment for deliberate concealment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: General compliance confirmation / register audit (mise à jour des registres sociaux)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least annually; confirmation upon any corporate event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalties for inaccurate records; administrative strike-off of the entity

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) mandatory if the SAS exceeds two of: balance sheet total > EUR 4,000,000; net turnover > EUR 8,000,000; average employees > 50. For an MMORPG with global revenue, audit is generally compulsory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Règlement ANC 2016-07) for legal entity statutory accounts; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial statements of publicly listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The UBO register must be maintained and filed with RCS annually together with the annual accounts; any shareholding transfer leading to UBO change must be updated and declared within 30 days of the change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registre des mandataires sociaux)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings (Registre des procès-verbaux)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 500 - EUR 2,500 annual registered office and corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 3,000 - EUR 12,000 annual statutory audit fee for a mid-size digital publishing entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on first €38,120 of taxable profit for SMEs; Research Tax Credit (CIR) up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) for SMEs; territoriality regime for foreign branches.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Corporate Income Tax Return) and annexes 2065-A to 2065-S; filed electronically via the impots.gouv.fr professional portal (EDI-TDFC).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For fiscal year ending 31 December, deadline is the second business day after 1 May. For other fiscal year-ends, within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income or loss after adjustments (reintegration of non-deductible expenses, application of tax credits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment must report French-source income; attach Form 2065-SD for branch accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net capital gains or losses on disposal of fixed assets, subject to specific rates (e.g., 12.8% for long-term gains on shares).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gains from French real estate or business assets; treaty may allocate taxing rights.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits (e.g., CIR, CII, foreign tax credits) to be offset against corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits for taxes paid on French-source income if treaty allows; attach Form 2065-CI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax reductions (e.g., for patronage, subsidies) that directly reduce the tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only applicable to French-source activities; non-residents may claim if eligible under domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 (Contribution sociale sur l'impôt sur les sociétés)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Additional social contribution of 3.3% on corporate income tax exceeding €763,000.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies to French permanent establishments; compute on the same taxable base.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% of tax due if filed within 30 days of deadline; 40% if after 30 days; 80% if tax evasion is established. Interest at 0.20% per month on unpaid tax. Additional penalties for failure to file annexes: €150 per missing document.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (standard rate for non-resident corporate shareholders; 30% for individuals; 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if holding ≥10% for 2 years and other conditions met).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced withholding tax under a tax treaty, the beneficial owner must submit Form 5000 (residence certificate) and Form 5001 (beneficial ownership declaration) to the French tax authorities before payment or within the statutory deadline. The foreign tax authority must certify the residence certificate. For EU/EEA entities, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies automatically if conditions are met; otherwise, treaty relief requires prior approval via the 'procédure de rescrit' (advance ruling) or refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 25% (or 33.33% for certain IP) reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive (if 25%+ ownership) or treaty rates (e.g., 0% under France-Germany treaty). Interest: statutory 30% (for non-resident lenders) reduced to 0% under EU Interest & Royalties Directive or treaty rates (e.g., 0% under France-UK treaty).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full Local File and Master File required if annual turnover or gross assets exceed €400 million; simplified documentation (Form 2257) required if turnover > €50 million and related-party transactions > €100,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not have a specific Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime, but applies general anti-abuse rules (e.g., Article 155-A CGI) and substance requirements for tax residency and treaty benefits. A French entity must have real economic activity (employees, premises, decision-making) to avoid challenges under the Principal Purpose Test (PPT) in tax treaties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income, false accounting, or concealment of revenue from in-app purchases (e.g., routing payments through offshore entities without economic substance).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of 80% of the evaded tax (if intentional) plus interest at 0.5% per month; criminal fines up to €500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 1741 CGI).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held jointly liable for corporate tax debts if they participated in fraudulent acts; travel bans and asset freezes possible; imprisonment up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting intercompany prices for IP royalties or services that do not reflect arm's length, shifting profits to low-tax jurisdictions without economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of taxable income, penalty of 40% (or 80% if abusive) on the adjustment, plus interest; potential criminal charges for tax fraud if intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation may face personal fines and imprisonment; civil liability for damages to the company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a shell entity with no real business activity, employees, or premises, used solely to hold IP or receive royalties to avoid French tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, 40% penalty for lack of substance, and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for unpaid taxes if the corporate veil is pierced; travel bans and extradition risks in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to implement anti-money laundering controls for in-app payment flows, or knowingly processing proceeds from illegal activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million for entities, criminal penalties for directors (up to 5 years imprisonment), and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment and fines; civil liability for damages to third parties.
